blogs.title: Meet BOFT: FFT-Inspired Finetuning That Cuts Parameters Without Cutting Performance
blogs.description: A plain-English overview of why adapting giant foundation models is hard, how Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) preserves pretrained knowledge, and how Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) slashes trainable parameters by moving from dense orthogonal matrices to FFT-inspired factorization.

blogs.title: Finetuning as Information Flow: A Visual Guide to BOFT’s Grid-and-Paths View
blogs.description: Explains the paper’s key perspective: composing a dense orthogonal matrix as information transmission across a layered graph. Walks through how sparse factors create dense connectivity, why this matters for parameter-efficiency, and how the butterfly topology achieves it elegantly.

blogs.title: Butterflies in the Weights: How FFT Structures Deliver O(d log d) Finetuning
blogs.description: Demystifies butterfly factorization using intuitive analogies to the Cooley–Tukey FFT. Shows how products of sparse, orthogonal ‘butterfly components’ build dense transformations with far fewer parameters, and why that’s a sweet spot for finetuning large models.

blogs.title: From OFT to BOFT: Expressivity, Regularity, and a Unified Orthogonal Framework
blogs.description: Explores how BOFT subsumes OFT: block-diagonal OFT as a special case, dense OFT as another, and BOFT as a smooth interpolation between them. Covers the b (block size) and m (depth) knobs, expressivity vs. generalization trade-offs, and the kaleidoscope hierarchy.

blogs.title: BOFT vs. LoRA vs. Adapters: Practical Trade-offs for LLMs, ViTs, and Diffusion
blogs.description: A practitioner’s comparison of popular PEFT methods. Highlights BOFT’s strengths (no inference latency, spectral stability, strong generalization) and when to choose it over LoRA or adapters based on task type, parameter budget, and deployment constraints.

blogs.title: Stability by Design: Orthogonality, Cayley Transforms, and Spectral Norms
blogs.description: Breaks down the math gently: why left-multiplying by an orthogonal matrix preserves spectral norms, how Cayley parameterization maintains orthogonality during training, and why this leads to stable, well-behaved finetuning.

blogs.title: BOFT in Practice: Initialization, Multiplicative Dropout, and Zero-Overhead Inference
blogs.description: Hands-on guidance for using BOFT: identity initialization, constructing orthogonal butterfly blocks, applying multiplicative dropout, choosing b and m, and merging factors into the base model to avoid inference overhead.

blogs.title: Limits and Horizons: Runtime Overheads, Better Topologies, and What Comes Next
blogs.description: Discusses the current limitations—extra training-time multiplies from factorization—and the paper’s call to explore new topologies from networking. Outlines research directions for faster training, adaptive structures, and broader domains.
